rows.note: Use 現場 as the all-purpose choice for the location of an event or what is happening there at the time.

example.english: You do not realize how chaotic the scene is until you get there
example.traditional: 你去到現場先知有幾混亂
example.jyutping: nei5 heoi3 dou3 jin6 coeng4 sin1 zi1 jau5 gei2 wan6 lyun6

rows.note: Use 一幕 for one distinct scene or section of a play, film, or other dramatic work.

example.english: The most moving scene in this film is when the main character says goodbye to his mother at the station.
example.traditional: 呢套戲最感人嘅一幕，就係主角喺車站同阿媽道別。
example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 hei3 zeoi3 gam2 jan4 ge3 jat1 mok6 zau6 hai6 zyu2 gok3 hai2 ce1 zaam6 tung4 aa3 maa1 dou6 bit6

rows.note: Use 圈子 for an informal social or interest-based circle such as the emo scene.

example.english: I am not really part of that scene
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 hai6 go2 go3 hyun1 zi2 ge3 jan4

rows.note: Use 風景 for a landscape or scenery viewed as a whole.

example.english: The scene here is so beautiful it looks like a painting
example.traditional: 呢度嘅風景真係靚到似畫
example.jyutping: ni1 dou6 ge3 fung1 ging2 zan1 hai6 leng3 dou3 ci5 waa2
